canonical_question: How does the presence of 27.3 nm Mn2O3 precipitates affect the yield strength compared to the strengthening provided by the 400 nm dislocation networks?

question_variants.question: How does the presence of 27.3 nm Mn2O3 precipitates affect the yield strength compared to the strengthening provided by the 400 nm dislocation networks?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper identifies the presence of 27.3 nm Mn2O3 precipitates and 400 nm dislocation networks as features contributing to mechanical properties but does not provide a quantitative comparison of the specific yield strength contribution of the precipitates versus the dislocation networks.

answers.answer: The study confirms the SLM-built HEA contains epitaxial growth grains, a dislocation network, and nano-sized oxides (27.3 nm Mn2O3) which collectively achieve outstanding mechanical properties. However, the text does not isolate or quantify the specific yield strength contribution of the Mn2O3 precipitates relative to the dislocation networks.
answers.measurement_outcome: Qualitative confirmation of outstanding mechanical properties due to fine grains, high dislocation density, and fine precipitates.
answers.mechanism: Fine grains, high dislocation density, and fine precipitates contribute to mechanical properties.
answers.boundary_limitation: No quantitative correlation model provided to separate strengthening contributions.
evidence_spans: SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution.
In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides.

Room- and high-temperature compression tests confirmed that SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties in all temperature ranges compared to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs reported up to the present.

source_evidence_spans: phases with an average size of 27.3 nm formed in the cell structure boundary
